- When sentiment is high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over 3–5 days, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for downward momentum.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or declining; apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias for days 1–7.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 85), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in correction.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model misreads momentum; use sentiment-weighted average for smoothing.
